version.changelog: Renamed from multi-agent-create. Added clawhub install, tags, interactive guided workflow.

llm.summary: The skill's behavior matches its stated purpose (creating agents and wiring channels), but its runtime instructions ask users to paste credentials and file paths into the agent chat and to run CLI login commands — practices that can expose secrets and are not clearly secured or constrained.

dimensions.detail: Name and description (create agents and connect messaging channels) align with the included helper script and SKILL.md; supported channels and workspace scaffolding are coherent with the stated goal.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md explicitly asks users to 'paste that token here' and to 'send me the path to the JSON file on this server' for Google Chat; it also instructs the agent to run CLI login commands (WhatsApp/Signal). Those instructions require the agent runtime to receive and handle sensitive secrets and local file paths. The skill gives no secure-storage guidance, no explicit handling for avoiding logging/exfiltration of secrets, and no constraint on where credentials will be written or how long they persist.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with a small helper shell script; no install spec, no external downloads, and included script content is readable. No high-risk installers or remote downloads present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, but the script reads OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR if present and operates on openclaw.json (the gateway config). The SKILL.md asks for many unrelated platform tokens (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Feishu, WhatsApp/Signal QR, Google service account path). Requesting multiple long-lived tokens and a service account JSON path is proportionate to configuring channel integrations, but the instructions ask that these secrets be pasted into the agent chat or given as file paths — this is risky and not documented as secure. There is no guidance about least-privilege tokens, token storage location, or rotation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-enabled and does not request elevated privileges. The included script backs up openclaw.json and creates files under the OpenClaw workspace; it does not modify other skills or system-wide settings beyond the user's OpenClaw config. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (normal), but combined with the secret-handling instructions this raises sensitivity of potential impact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says, but it asks you to supply sensitive tokens and even local file paths to the agent runtime. Before installing or using it: (1) do NOT paste long-lived credentials into chat logs — instead add them directly to your gateway config file with appropriate file permissions, or use short-lived/least-privilege tokens; (2) if you must paste a token, ensure the agent runtime will not log or transmit it elsewhere and rotate the token after use; (3) avoid sending paths to sensitive JSON key files — copy necessary keys into a restricted directory and reference them locally; (4) review ./scripts/setup-agent.sh to confirm it writes credentials where you expect (the script currently only creates workspace files and backs up openclaw.json but does not write channel tokens itself); (5) when using CLI login commands (WhatsApp/Signal), run them in a trusted terminal session; and (6) consider creating per-bot/limited-scope credentials and rotating them after onboarding. If you need higher assurance, request the skill author to add explicit secure-storage guidance (or an option to open a local prompt that writes credentials directly to the config file without appearing in conversation history).
